Columbia University
United States · Mathematics PhD

Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; Fall 2026 exception is not a confirmed Fall 2027 waiver.
• Central and department document/score timing differ; use earlier date until confirmed.
• UChicago English exemption explicitly requires at least two years at an American institution.
• Lue Pan and Lucas Mason-Brown are new Columbia faculty for 2026-27.

postdoctoral appointments are not treated as ordinary permanent PhD advisers. Recent-paper coverage
remains incomplete for de Jong and Thaddeus.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible to apply with a UChicago bachelor’s degree earned or expected before entry; international students
explicitly welcome. A master’s is not a prerequisite. F-1 status does not itself establish academic eligibility.
[s15] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Arrange three academic letters, unofficial transcripts, resume, two essays and required Math GRE. Only one
GSAS PhD application per term. Recommenders should know Re Vera may authenticate letters. Apply for a fee
waiver after submission and before payment if needed. [s1] [s5] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor agreement required in reviewed admissions checklist. Use faculty pages to make focused
research inquiries; confirm 2027 advising capacity. Lue Pan and Lucas Mason-Brown joined Columbia for
2026-27; older Princeton/UT Austin affiliation pages are stale. [s1] [s17]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
One GSAS PhD application per term. Electronic uploads/letters; applicant submits own application. Status
checklist and corrections/additions upload available after submission. No account or referee invitation was
created for this research. [s5] [s6] [s11]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 application and 2 December 2026 deadline explicitly published; GRE scheduling waiver text still Fall
2026. Funding figures currently 2026-27 rather than 2027-28. [s1] [s8] [s12]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
2 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. [s1] [s4]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
All PhD applicants automatically considered for institutional funding through admission; no additional funding
application. External fellowships have independent deadlines. [s6] [s14]

Reference receipt [Conflict]
Aim for 2 December 2026. Central GSAS allows letters up to two weeks afterward: 16 December 2026 is the
calculated date; time not separately stated. Later letters appended but review not guaranteed. Department
says required materials by posted deadline, so ask about this discrepancy rather than relying on grace. [s4] [s5]
[s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Central GSAS: official scores within two weeks of deadline (calculated 16 December 2026). Department FAQ
says November Math GRE received by January 1 is not disadvantageous, without a current cycle year. These
conflict; arrange official delivery by 16 December or obtain department confirmation. [s5] [s15] [s2]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Application uploads by 2 December 2026. Central FAQ permits supporting documents within two weeks for
deadlines before May 1; department asks all required materials by deadline. Use 2 December for
applicant-controlled uploads. [s3] [s4] [s6]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics/GSAS-specific 2027 acceptance deadline established in targeted official searches. Read the
individual offer and any interim response requirement; do not import another Columbia department’s date. [s1]
[s6]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL 100 for tests before 21 January 2026 or 5.5 on new scale; IELTS Academic 7.5 or DET 135.
Scores valid two years. Subsequent ALP writing/oral teaching assessments may still be assigned. [s15]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
No English test or waiver form needed if UChicago undergraduate degree has been or will soon be awarded
and at least two years were studied at an American university. This explicit two-year condition matters for
transfer students. [s15]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required in GSAS checklist; department recommends it. This is optional-but-recommended, not forbidden
or ignored. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Required. Published inability-to-schedule waiver paragraph is expressly for Fall 2026, even though deadline is
now 2027 cycle. Do not assume it extends to Fall 2027; ask if needed. [s1] [s2]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload transcripts covering all university academic work, one PDF per institution in Educational History; include
institution identification and grading legend. Under 2 MB; recommend under 300 dpi and legible at US-letter
size. Official records after accepting an offer, with credential verification. [s5] [s10]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
Separate mathematics-course list not listed as a Math requirement. Central course-list rule explicitly names
other programs, not Mathematics. No math-specific template, limits or upload rule established; inspect current
portal before assuming an extra list is permitted. [s1] [s5]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate course-description requirement found in mathematics/GSAS checklist. Any optional upload
permission and limits remain unverified. [s1] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three academic letters in mathematics program checklist. Central minimum is two academic, maximum four
total and at most one professional. For a current undergraduate use three academic references to satisfy the
stricter department wording. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No extra reference for automatic institutional PhD funding identified. Outside award requirements remain
award-specific. [s14]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
GSAS sends email submission instructions; FAQ discusses excluding/reentering a referee and a new email
before application submission. This supports pre-submission requests, but exact entry-versus-Send-button
trigger is not publicly established. [s5] [s6]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Applicant may submit before letters arrive. Requests can operate before final submission; they are not
restricted to after submission. [s5] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Email confirms receipt; post-submission status checklist tracks letters. Electronic individual submissions
required; no emailed/posted letters. Electronic Interfolio/career-office delivery accepted via each unique
referee link. [s5] [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Reapplicants using the same account may include previous letters. Before a letter is filed, exclude/reenter
referee to correct FERPA selection. After submission, waiver may be added through documented email/upload
process but cannot be rescinded. Replacement of an already filed letter’s content is not publicly established.
[s5] [s6]

Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required CV/resume upload. No public math-specific page limit or typography requirement found; follow
current upload control. [s1] [s11]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required uploaded academic statement, maximum 1,000 words; no other required formatting. Prompt faithful
paraphrase: academic background and past work in intended field, graduate-study plans at Columbia, and
future career goals. [s6] [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required upload, 500-1,000 words in FAQ; dedicated prompt says maximum 1,000. No other formatting
prescribed. Prompt faithful paraphrase: explain personal history/experiences and the perspectives and
contributions you would bring to the entering class and Columbia community. [s6] [s7]

Describe study plans within academic SOP. No separate research-interest essay/limit found. [s6] [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2027-28 mathematics cash offer not published. Department describes a nine-month fellowship stipend plus
tuition exemption. University 2026-27 benchmarks: no appointment $37,506 nine-month + $6,753 summer =
$44,259; with appointment $38,256 + $6,753 = $45,009. Twelve-month benchmarks $50,008/$51,008
respectively. These are institutional benchmarks, not a confirmed 2027 math award. Central PhD package
includes tuition and health; department notes some student activity/transcript fees may remain. [s3] [s12] [s6]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five-year fellowship for all admitted mathematics PhD students, conditional on satisfactory progress. Verify
exact summer coverage and later-year teaching duties in offer. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD admits eligible for the same tuition/health/living support; citizenship does not exclude
institutional funding. [s6] [s14]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Good academic standing/progress required. Department describes tuition exemption, stipend and eligibility for
university housing; some non-tuition fees may remain. Appointment duties and summer conditions should be
stated in offer. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No additional institutional funding application required. [s6] [s14]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
Outside fellowships encouraged; departmental policy supplements outside funds to institutional level unless
award terms prohibit. GSAS external-fellowship policy publishes a $6,000 top-off and offset formulas; its
2026-27 base figures differ from September 2026 compensation update. Ask which rate governs; do not add
two full stipends. [s3] [s13] [s12]
Application fee [2027 confirmed]
US $125 for the 2027 application, nonrefundable; credit card (Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover). File incomplete
until payment or approved waiver. [s8]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
After submitting application, request through Applicant Status with supporting hardship documents; do not pay
while pending. Financial-need wording has no stated citizenship exclusion. Usually 5-7 business days;
maximum two lifetime GSAS waivers. Research-pathway/event and named agency sponsorship routes also
exist. If denied, pay before completion. No distinct published request cutoff found. [s9]

text:
Columbia University
United States · Mathematics PhD
2026 US News roster/rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; Fall 2026 exception is not a confirmed Fall 2027 waiver.
• Central and department document/score timing differ; use earlier date until confirmed.
• UChicago English exemption explicitly requires at least two years at an American institution.
• Lue Pan and Lucas Mason-Brown are new Columbia faculty for 2026-27.
• Historical research-area pages list faculty absent from current roster; this shortlist uses current bulletin. Ritt
postdoctoral appointments are not treated as ordinary permanent PhD advisers. Recent-paper coverage
remains incomplete for de Jong and Thaddeus.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible to apply with a UChicago bachelor’s degree earned or expected before entry; international students
explicitly welcome. A master’s is not a prerequisite. F-1 status does not itself establish academic eligibility.
[s15] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Arrange three academic letters, unofficial transcripts, resume, two essays and required Math GRE. Only one
GSAS PhD application per term. Recommenders should know Re Vera may authenticate letters. Apply for a fee
waiver after submission and before payment if needed. [s1] [s5] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor agreement required in reviewed admissions checklist. Use faculty pages to make focused
research inquiries; confirm 2027 advising capacity. Lue Pan and Lucas Mason-Brown joined Columbia for
2026-27; older Princeton/UT Austin affiliation pages are stale. [s1] [s17]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
One GSAS PhD application per term. Electronic uploads/letters; applicant submits own application. Status
checklist and corrections/additions upload available after submission. No account or referee invitation was
created for this research. [s5] [s6] [s11]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027 application and 2 December 2026 deadline explicitly published; GRE scheduling waiver text still Fall
2026. Funding figures currently 2026-27 rather than 2027-28. [s1] [s8] [s12]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
2 December 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. [s1] [s4]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
All PhD applicants automatically considered for institutional funding through admission; no additional funding
application. External fellowships have independent deadlines. [s6] [s14]

Reference receipt [Conflict]
Aim for 2 December 2026. Central GSAS allows letters up to two weeks afterward: 16 December 2026 is the
calculated date; time not separately stated. Later letters appended but review not guaranteed. Department
says required materials by posted deadline, so ask about this discrepancy rather than relying on grace. [s4] [s5]
[s3]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Central GSAS: official scores within two weeks of deadline (calculated 16 December 2026). Department FAQ
says November Math GRE received by January 1 is not disadvantageous, without a current cycle year. These
conflict; arrange official delivery by 16 December or obtain department confirmation. [s5] [s15] [s2]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Application uploads by 2 December 2026. Central FAQ permits supporting documents within two weeks for
deadlines before May 1; department asks all required materials by deadline. Use 2 December for
applicant-controlled uploads. [s3] [s4] [s6]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
No mathematics/GSAS-specific 2027 acceptance deadline established in targeted official searches. Read the
individual offer and any interim response requirement; do not import another Columbia department’s date. [s1]
[s6]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL 100 for tests before 21 January 2026 or 5.5 on new scale; IELTS Academic 7.5 or DET 135.
Scores valid two years. Subsequent ALP writing/oral teaching assessments may still be assigned. [s15]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
No English test or waiver form needed if UChicago undergraduate degree has been or will soon be awarded
and at least two years were studied at an American university. This explicit two-year condition matters for
transfer students. [s15]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required in GSAS checklist; department recommends it. This is optional-but-recommended, not forbidden
or ignored. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Required. Published inability-to-schedule waiver paragraph is expressly for Fall 2026, even though deadline is
now 2027 cycle. Do not assume it extends to Fall 2027; ask if needed. [s1] [s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload transcripts covering all university academic work, one PDF per institution in Educational History; include
institution identification and grading legend. Under 2 MB; recommend under 300 dpi and legible at US-letter
size. Official records after accepting an offer, with credential verification. [s5] [s10]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
Separate mathematics-course list not listed as a Math requirement. Central course-list rule explicitly names
other programs, not Mathematics. No math-specific template, limits or upload rule established; inspect current
portal before assuming an extra list is permitted. [s1] [s5]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
No separate course-description requirement found in mathematics/GSAS checklist. Any optional upload
permission and limits remain unverified. [s1] [s5]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three academic letters in mathematics program checklist. Central minimum is two academic, maximum four
total and at most one professional. For a current undergraduate use three academic references to satisfy the
stricter department wording. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No extra reference for automatic institutional PhD funding identified. Outside award requirements remain
award-specific. [s14]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
GSAS sends email submission instructions; FAQ discusses excluding/reentering a referee and a new email
before application submission. This supports pre-submission requests, but exact entry-versus-Send-button
trigger is not publicly established. [s5] [s6]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Applicant may submit before letters arrive. Requests can operate before final submission; they are not
restricted to after submission. [s5] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Email confirms receipt; post-submission status checklist tracks letters. Electronic individual submissions
required; no emailed/posted letters. Electronic Interfolio/career-office delivery accepted via each unique
referee link. [s5] [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Reapplicants using the same account may include previous letters. Before a letter is filed, exclude/reenter
referee to correct FERPA selection. After submission, waiver may be added through documented email/upload
process but cannot be rescinded. Replacement of an already filed letter’s content is not publicly established.
[s5] [s6]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required CV/resume upload. No public math-specific page limit or typography requirement found; follow
current upload control. [s1] [s11]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required uploaded academic statement, maximum 1,000 words; no other required formatting. Prompt faithful
paraphrase: academic background and past work in intended field, graduate-study plans at Columbia, and
future career goals. [s6] [s1]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Required upload, 500-1,000 words in FAQ; dedicated prompt says maximum 1,000. No other formatting
prescribed. Prompt faithful paraphrase: explain personal history/experiences and the perspectives and
contributions you would bring to the entering class and Columbia community. [s6] [s7]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Describe study plans within academic SOP. No separate research-interest essay/limit found. [s6] [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list [Unresolved]
Not listed as a required standalone mathematics document in current program checklist. No public
optional-upload permission, prompt, limit, or paper-versus-link rule established. GSAS will not append
unsolicited materials sent outside the application. [s1] [s11] [s6]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
Separate mathematics-course list not listed as a Math requirement. Central course-list rule explicitly names

other programs, not Mathematics. No math-specific template, limits or upload rule established; inspect current
portal before assuming an extra list is permitted. [s1] [s5]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No additional institutional-funding essay identified because consideration is automatic. External award essays
must be checked separately. [s6] [s14]
Other short answers / materials [Conflict]
GRE exception, if department confirms it applies for 2027, uses Additional Information and Supplementary
Media; public wording currently says Fall 2026. Credential-verification Authorization and Release Form is
required. No word limit published for exception explanation. [s1] [s10]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2027-28 mathematics cash offer not published. Department describes a nine-month fellowship stipend plus
tuition exemption. University 2026-27 benchmarks: no appointment $37,506 nine-month + $6,753 summer =
$44,259; with appointment $38,256 + $6,753 = $45,009. Twelve-month benchmarks $50,008/$51,008
respectively. These are institutional benchmarks, not a confirmed 2027 math award. Central PhD package
includes tuition and health; department notes some student activity/transcript fees may remain. [s3] [s12] [s6]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Five-year fellowship for all admitted mathematics PhD students, conditional on satisfactory progress. Verify
exact summer coverage and later-year teaching duties in offer. [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International PhD admits eligible for the same tuition/health/living support; citizenship does not exclude
institutional funding. [s6] [s14]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Good academic standing/progress required. Department describes tuition exemption, stipend and eligibility for
university housing; some non-tuition fees may remain. Appointment duties and summer conditions should be
stated in offer. [s3]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No additional institutional funding application required. [s6] [s14]
Other funding routes [Conflict]
Outside fellowships encouraged; departmental policy supplements outside funds to institutional level unless
award terms prohibit. GSAS external-fellowship policy publishes a $6,000 top-off and offset formulas; its
2026-27 base figures differ from September 2026 compensation update. Ask which rate governs; do not add
two full stipends. [s3] [s13] [s12]
Application fee [2027 confirmed]
US $125 for the 2027 application, nonrefundable; credit card (Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover). File incomplete
until payment or approved waiver. [s8]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
After submitting application, request through Applicant Status with supporting hardship documents; do not pay
while pending. Financial-need wording has no stated citizenship exclusion. Usually 5-7 business days;
maximum two lifetime GSAS waivers. Research-pathway/event and named agency sponsorship routes also
exist. If denied, pay before completion. No distinct published request cutoff found. [s9]

Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Department all-documents-by-deadline rule versus central two-week grace; department January 1 GRE
tolerance versus central two-week official-score deadline; 2027 deadline beside Fall 2026 GRE exception;
external-fellowship base rates versus newer compensation rates; program asks three academic letters while
central minimum is two. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5] [s12] [s13]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm 2027 GRE exception, permitted late-score/reference dates, exact referee trigger and replacement
policy, portal-only supplementary-document slots, current math stipend/summer/fees, and offer reply date.
Check current advising availability, especially leave/joint appointments. [s1] [s2] [s5] [s6] [s12] [s16]
